Definition: Conanjah, the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Cononiah — spelled Conaniah in 2 Chronicles 35:9 — was a Levite ruler under Hezekiah, set over the offerings and tithes brought into the temple in 2 Chronicles 31:12, with overseers working under his hand in 2 Chronicles 31:13. In Josiah's day another Conaniah, chief of the Levites, gave five thousand passover offerings in 2 Chronicles 35:9.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe men like Cononiah are the quiet backbone of the story: no speeches, no miracles, just faithful oversight of what God's people brought, so the work of the house could go on.
RelatedPeople: Cononiah, Chief of the Levites; Cononiah, the Levite; King Hezekiah
